title: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs (umbrella)
creator: Marcus Lin
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: KMS hardening + rotation
description:
Umbrella issue for Redwood’s KMS integration hardening + key rotation + failure-mode testing + documentation rollout across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Context / why now
- Enterprise security reviews (esp. Private) keep landing on: customer-managed KMS support clarity, predictable rotation with minimal downtime, and evidence/auditability.
- Our current integrations work but have gaps: inconsistent key selection behavior during rollouts, limited resilience to KMS brownouts, and rotation procedures that are not sufficiently deterministic/repeatable for Private operators.
- Goal is to reduce blast radius for key compromise/misconfiguration, make rotation boring, and prove resilience with systematic tests + runbooks.

Primary goals (what “done” looks like)
1) Safer key hierarchy / envelope encryption contracts
   - Clear KEK/DEK usage boundaries and caching rules in both control plane and data plane.
   - Deterministic key selection and explicit key version pinning (no accidental drift during config migrations or rollout changes).
   - Backwards compatibility: all existing ciphertext remains decryptable throughout the rollout and after upgrade.

2) Predictable rotation (scheduled + emergency)
   - Operators can execute scheduled rotation with a documented, low-downtime workflow.
   - Emergency rotation is supported with tighter timelines and explicit rollback constraints.
   - Private: supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault where applicable) with clear shared-responsibility boundaries.

3) Resilience to KMS failures + validated behavior
   - Data plane includes standardized retry/backoff + circuit breaker behavior, with SLO-aligned thresholds and safe defaults.
   - Failure-mode harness can simulate: timeouts, throttling, IAM denies, disabled keys, provider/API/region outages.
   - Game day(s) executed with a written test plan, observed results, and follow-up fixes tracked.

4) Audit logging and evidence
   - Structured audit events for key lifecycle + KMS operations (incl. denials/failures) are emitted to the audit pipeline.
   - Evidence mapping is documented for GRC (Olga’s team), with retention expectations and “how to answer” customer Qs.

Scope
In scope:
- Control-plane config for KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS; Azure Key Vault where applicable in Private).
- Data-plane encrypt/decrypt paths: DEK/KEK usage, caching + TTLs, retry/backoff/circuit breaking.
- Rotation workflows: scheduled + emergency; dual-read window; (optional) re-encryption orchestration where applicable.
- Audit logging requirements + schema + integration.
- Operator docs (Confluence + public docs), troubleshooting, and customer-facing security FAQ deltas.
- Repeatable test harness + game-day execution.

Out of scope:
- Replacing cryptographic primitives wholesale.
- Adding entirely new storage backends.
- Breaking changes to ciphertext formats without explicit migration/compat plan.

Milestones & rough schedule (6–8 weeks)
Week 1 (Assessment + design)
- Threat model + architecture overview; define explicit misuse cases and mitigations.
- Write ADR for rotation semantics + backwards compat contract.

Weeks 2–5 (Implementation)
- Control plane: key selection + version pinning + config validation.
- Data plane: standardized retry/backoff + circuit breaker; caching rules and safe defaults.
- Rotation plumbing: dual-read window + bounded fallback; validation hooks.
- Audit events: schema and pipeline integration.
- Private installer: KMS preflight checks + clearer error messaging.

Weeks 4–7 (Failure-mode validation + ops readiness)
- Build failure-mode test harness; execute matrix in staging.
- Run at least one structured game day; capture learnings + harden.
- Produce runbooks + on-call playbooks; alert tuning.

Weeks 6–8 (Docs + phased rollout)
- Publish Private operator rotation procedure + troubleshooting.
- Update customer-facing docs/FAQ and enterprise response collateral.
- Gradual rollout: Private (new installs first), then opt-in upgrades, then broaden defaults across Hosted/Dedicated.

Workstreams / linked issues (sub-issues)
- ENG-4221: Deterministic key selection + version pinning rules in control plane config.
- ENG-4226: Circuit breaker + adaptive backoff for KMS calls in data plane.
- ENG-4230: Rotation workflow implementation (dual-read window, re-encryption orchestration where applicable, validation hooks).
- ENG-4234: Failure-mode test plan + harness; acceptance criteria.
- ENG-4239: Observability (metrics/tracing, cache hit rates, breaker state, per-tenant summaries).
- ENG-4242: Private installer KMS validation + preflight checks.
- ENG-4246: Docs tracking (rotation procedure, troubleshooting guide, security FAQ deltas).
- ENG-4251: Security review: least-privilege IAM templates per provider; key policy guidance; breakglass requirements.
- ENG-4258: Game day execution issue (staging + one canary) + follow-ups.

Rollout plan (proposed)
Phase 0: Behind flags in staging
- All behavior-changing code paths gated (key selection/pinning, breaker defaults, dual-read rotation logic).
- Failure injection hooks enabled only in staging.

Phase 1: Private first (new installs)
- New Private installs default to pinned key version selection + validated config.
- Installer preflight checks required (explicitly fail fast on missing IAM/KMS permissions).

Phase 2: Private opt-in upgrades
- Existing Private customers can opt-in to rotation workflow + dual-read behavior.
- Provide customer-facing checklist + rollback guidance.

Phase 3: Hosted/Dedicated broaden defaults
- Gradually enable safer defaults for hosted tenants.
- Canary → small % → broad, with guardrails + automatic rollback criteria.

Success metrics / acceptance criteria
- Rotation completes with no customer-visible outage for the documented “scheduled rotation” path under normal KMS behavior.
- Under KMS brownout scenarios (timeouts/throttles), services degrade predictably (bounded error rates), breaker opens, and alerting triggers with actionable signals.
- Under IAM AccessDenied or disabled keys, behavior is explicit: fast-fail with clear errors + audit events; runbook includes mitigation/triage steps.
- Audit events emitted for key lifecycle and KMS operation failures/denials; GRC can map evidence to controls.

Risks / open questions
- Performance impact: extra KMS calls if cache TTL too low or dual-read window too aggressive. Need explicit perf budgets and observability.
- Provider differences: key version semantics differ across AWS/GCP/Azure; pinning rules must remain intuitive for operators.
- Backwards compatibility: ensure ciphertext produced pre-change remains decryptable even during emergency rotation scenarios.
- Alert fatigue: balance early detection with paging policy; tune thresholds after game day.

References / artifacts
- Confluence: KMS integration hardening overview (security + threat model)
- ADR: KMS rotation contracts and backwards compat
- Runbook: KMS dependency degradation (SRE)

Release coordination notes

- Require sign-offs before broad enablement: Security (Marcus), SRE (Sean), Control plane (Ethan), Docs (Elliot), GRC (Olga) for evidence language.
